what: ING Groep is a Dutch bank. It is the leading bank in the Netherlands and Belgium and runs a large digital-only retail bank in Germany, Spain, Poland and Australia, plus wholesale banking for European corporates.
customers: Retail customers across ten European markets and Australia, and corporate and institutional clients in Europe.
money: current accounts, savings and mortgages across Europe
corporate lending, trade finance and financial markets
moat: A digital-only model with no branches in most markets, giving it a cost advantage over incumbent banks that still run branch networks.
risks: European Central Bank rate cuts lower income on its deposit base
Dutch and Belgian mortgage competition is intense
Debt funding of about $203 billion makes it sensitive to wholesale markets
Anti-money-laundering compliance has cost it fines in the past
opportunities: Revenue grew about 38% last year as rates lifted deposit income
Return on invested capital near 35% is high for a European bank
It returns capital through large buybacks alongside a dividend above 4%
watch: Net interest income as European rates fall, and fee income growth.
